import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Define a custom order for age groups to ensure logical plotting
age_group_order = ["18-24", "25-34", "35-44", "45-54", "55+"]
df['customer_age_group'] = pd.Categorical(df['customer_age_group'], categories=age_group_order, ordered=True)

# Aggregate total sales by product and customer age group
sales_by_product_age = df.groupby(['product', 'customer_age_group'])['total'].sum().reset_index()

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the grouped bar chart
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8))
sns.barplot(
    data=sales_by_product_age,
    x='product',
    y='total',
    hue='customer_age_group',
    palette='viridis',
    errorbar=None  # We are plotting sums, so error bars are not applicable
)

# Add labels and title for clarity
plt.title('Total Sales by Product and Customer Age Group', fontsize=18, weight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Product', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=14)
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=12) # Rotate x-axis labels for better readability
plt.yticks(fontsize=12)

# Place the legend outside the plot to avoid obscuring data
plt.legend(title='Customer Age Group', title_fontsize='13', fontsize='11',
           bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels/legend from being cut off
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.98, 1]) # Adjust rect to make space for the legend

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
